To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cycling progenitors maintain the epidermis and intestine, while differentiating cells can also contribute to repair.
cycling cells contribute to epithelial repair.
the maintenance of epithelial homeostatic turnover is achieved by a balance of cell divisions that are symmetric and asymmetric, and that this balance is maintained across the population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular and molecular mechanisms that regulate tissue homeostasis, and how these are altered in disease.
how the balance between proliferation and differentiation is regulated, how the balance is maintained across the population of progenitors and how this is altered in response to tissue damage.
the cellular and molecular mechanisms that control the balance of self‐renewing and differentiating progenitor cells in epithelial homeostatic and repair responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epithelial homeostatic model has been extended to encompass a population of progenitor cells that undergo stochastic cell fate determination.
the epithelial stem cell is not a single, defined cell but a population that can be maintained by a variety of mechanisms, depending on the tissue and the injury.
epithelial stem and progenitor populations are not homogeneous but are heterogeneous, and that they can self‐renew and contribute to tissue repair.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stem cell concept is not a universal paradigm for epithelial homeostatic maintenance, but rather a tissue‐specific property.

stem cells are not the only cell types that can contribute to tissue maintenance, and that the contribution to tissue maintenance of cycling progenitors and differentiated cells depends on the tissue and the type of damage.
the epithelial stem and progenitor cell compartments have evolved independently in different epithelial organs, and are not interchangeable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cycling cells can contribute to repair, and that the contribution of different cell types varies between tissues and in response to different types of injury.
cycling progenitors maintain epithelial tissues, and that stem cells are not essential for tissue homeostasis or regeneration.
the stem cell concept is a useful tool for understanding epithelial maintenance, but it should not be used as a model for regeneration.
